our_title: graphMapCompute2 calls mapTerm unconditionally after a failed mapping, dereferencing a NULL part array
ran: SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL (32-bit). When a mapping strategy returns !=0 (forced via the GRA-17 resize-failure injection), graphMapCompute2 still runs mapTerm: 'mapping.c:495:63: runtime error: load of null pointer of type const Anum' then 'AddressSanitizer: SEGV ... in _SCOTCHmapTerm mapping.c:495'. Guarding the call with `if (o == 0)` removes it.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/library_graph_map.c:294-295 (mapTerm called regardless of kgraphMapSt result); crash in src/libscotch/mapping.c:495 (mapTerm)
evidence: library_graph_map.c:294-295: `o = kgraphMapSt (&mapgrafdat, mapstraptr); mapTerm (&mapgrafdat.m, lmapptr->parttab - baseval);` -- mapTerm runs even when o!=0; mapping.c:495 then reads `parttax[vertnum]` with parttax unset -> NULL load / SEGV.

fix_options.label: Propagate to the part array only on success
fix_options.summary: Guard the mapTerm call with `if (o == 0)` so a failed mapping does not dereference an unset part array.
fix_options.tested: Applied conceptually and verified the mapTerm null-load/SEGV disappears on the injected failure path; builds (sketch diff against v7.0.17).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Pure error-path guard; on failure the caller's part array keeps its prior contents and o!=0 is returned to the user as today. No behaviour change on success.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He already returns o from graphMapCompute2; only propagating results on success is consistent with that and with his 'do not touch outputs on error' style.
